findings.title: Recovery codes are not consumed after use
findings.body: In isValid() for recovery codes, the provided code is only compared against the stored raw codes, but it is not marked as used or removed. As a result, the same recovery code can be reused multiple times, defeating the purpose of recovery codes. This differs from the local storage implementation, which consumes the code after successful validation. The test provider should update its stored credential to remove or mark the used code, and the test should verify that a used code cannot be used again.

findings.title: Recovery codes credential ID not preserved in getCredentials
findings.body: In getCredentials(), the recovery codes credential model is reconstructed from raw codes using RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromValues(), which generates a new ID. The original ID stored in myUser.recoveryCodes is lost. If the authenticator later determines that all codes have been used and attempts to remove the credential via removeStoredCredentialById(), it will use the newly generated ID, which does not match the stored credential ID, causing the removal to fail. This also prevents proper usage tracking because the returned model always appears to have all codes available.
